answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties later attest were delivered correctly; new identities start with no weight, and each attestation is backed by a refundable stake that is forfeited if a fraud dispute is upheld. A Sybil operator must therefore fund many separate stakes and produce useful work across unrelated counterparties, rather than cheaply minting accounts. A tundra survey or walnut grove inventory might attract clients, but the names alone buy no influence.
